title: Cohomology of abelian sheaves on a finite-dimensional spectral space
statement:
Let $T$ be a spectral topological space [def-weil-spectral-space], let $d\geq0$ be an integer, and suppose its topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is at most $d$. For every sheaf $F$ of abelian groups on $T$, with cohomology the right-derived global sections in abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology],
$$H^q(T,F)=0\qquad(q>d).$$
The empty space is included, with dimension $-\infty$. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral, part (1) (lines 3940–3948); with an upper bound d in place of the exact dimension.

proof.text: Induct on the natural-number upper bound d, retaining vanishing for all sheaves and all degrees greater than d. At d=0, any proper inclusion of two irreducible point closures contradicts the dimension bound, so T0 implies T1. The proved spectral T1 characterization (Stacks Topology 0905) gives a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space, and profinite vanishing gives all positive degrees, including the empty case.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral; finite-cover Mayer-Vietoris version of the proof of (1) from (2), and Tag 01EB.

proof.text: At bound n+1 and compact open U, put Z=X\U. The punctured generalization subspace S is spectral and has dimension at most n. Apply the induction hypothesis to the inverse-image abelian sheaf on S in degree n+1.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral; finite-cover Mayer-Vietoris version of the proof of (1) from (2), and Tag 01EB.

proof.text: The canonical punctured-neighborhood cocone is a colimit by the existing comparison theorem. Its vertex is zero by the preceding step. The stage N=X is U. Mathlib Limits.IsColimit.eq_iff' gives a smaller neighborhood V of Z on which the given class restricts to zero on U intersect V. This uses the same-universe general concrete filtered-colimit criterion, avoiding the older universe-u+1 wrapper.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral; finite-cover Mayer-Vietoris version of the proof of (1) from (2), and Tag 01EB.

proof.text: The opens U and V cover X. Apply Mathlib's GrothendieckTopology.MayerVietorisSquare.sequence_exact to Opens.mayerVietorisSquare U V directly for abelian-sheaf Ext cohomology. The pair (x,0) has zero difference on the intersection, hence lifts to X. Thus degree n+1 restriction from X onto every compact open is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral; finite-cover Mayer-Vietoris version of the proof of (1) from (2), and Tag 01EB.

proof.text: Every positive cohomology class x on an open vanishes locally: efface x by an epimorphism G onto the free abelian sheaf of the open, lift its universal section locally using local surjectivity of an epimorphism of abelian sheaves, and use the sheafification/free/Yoneda adjunction to factor the smaller free-open map through G. Associativity of Ext composition kills the restriction.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral; finite-cover Mayer-Vietoris version of the proof of (1) from (2), and Tag 01EB.

proof.text: For a global degree n+2 class, refine local zero neighborhoods to compact opens and take a finite subcover. Induct on finite unions of that cover. For two opens, the Mayer-Vietoris sequence makes restriction in degree n+2 injective when the degree n+1 restriction to their intersection is surjective. The intersection is compact open by spectrality; restriction onto it from X is surjective by step 4 and factors through either member, so the required surjectivity holds. The class therefore vanishes on each finite union and hence on X. The empty-union base follows because the free abelian sheaf of the empty open is projective: every section group of a sheaf on the empty open is zero.

source.place: Tag 0A3G, proposition-cohomological-dimension-spectral; finite-cover Mayer-Vietoris version of the proof of (1) from (2), and Tag 01EB.

proof.text: For every larger degree, embed F into an injective I and use the short exact sequence with its cokernel Q. Positive Ext into I vanishes; the Ext long exact sequence expresses any class of F as the boundary of a class of Q one degree lower. Induction on degree, starting at n+2 from step 6, proves all degrees above n+1. This closes the dimension induction and specializes to d.
